column1: # The values the bots' chat puts into a line, in Turkish, for a reader whose client
# names Turkish (Said, saido_0, 21 October; his chat_values_tr.tsv as he sent it,
# Said-TR-names-chat-20261021, the format rows after it, and the rows of his
# reply the same day, english-values-for-said.tr.tsv, at the end). The core reads it
# with the libraries (playerbot_live_chat.h; the rules are
# playerbot_chat_value_rules.h): wherever a line of playerbot_live_chat_tr.tsv
# would say the English value of a placeholder, it says this file's instead, and
# the English where the file has no row. ASCII, as the libraries are.
# The placeholder's own rows are looked up by the English value (en), not by the
# key - the key says what Said rendered the row from: a skill's vnum, a skrot's
# item vnums. Items, monsters and NPCs are playerbot_live_chat_names_tr.tsv.
# "format" rows are Turkish word order for a value made of parts, the key the
# placeholder they apply to: {n} is a number, {x} the rest, said by that
# placeholder's own rows. From Said's notes: "Turkish puts % first" (bon, and the
# event's "+50% experience" the same way) and "<item> <n> bonuses" ->
# "<n> efsunlu <item>"; and from his reply the trade's "10crit" -> "10 kritik"
# and a wish's "30% avg+" -> "%30+ ort". A format is tried on the whole value
# and then on each run of its pieces between spaces and commas.
